sampling_model.design: Independent and identically distributed observational sampling from an unrestricted binary-treatment law; the explicit posterior theorem specializes to \(X\sim\mathrm{Unif}[0,1]\) and \(e(x)=x\).
sampling_model.treatment: Binary treatment with unknown observational propensity \(e(x)\); the intervention uses \(q_\delta(1\mid x)=\min\{1,\delta e(x)\}\).
sampling_model.overlap: Strong overlap is not assumed. The policy preserves observational support, and the histogram benchmark has essential propensity infimum zero and essential supremum one.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: All observations update independent Beta histogram coordinates for the propensity and two arm-specific Bernoulli regressions on \(J_n=\lceil n^{1/3}\rceil\) equal bins; independent Dirichlet Bayesian-bootstrap weights perform the one-step correction.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The paper studies the intervention \(\min\{1,e^\delta\pi(x)\}\) and develops identification and estimation of its interventional effects.
The optimal-value parameter is pathwise differentiable if and only if its stated exceptional-law variance condition holds.
Smooth incremental propensity-score interventions admit a nonparametric efficient influence function and efficient one-step estimation without positivity.
Uniform no-bias, \(L_2\)-stability, and empirical-process conditions imply a semiparametric one-step posterior Bernstein--von Mises theorem.

For twice continuously differentiable stochastic intervention maps with stable influence functions, the corrected posterior is asymptotically efficient and its credible intervals have pointwise frequentist coverage.
Dirichlet random histograms attain the optimal sup-norm posterior contraction rate for Hölder densities.
A margin condition controls nonsmooth branch selection and permits root-\(n\) influence-function inference for covariate-assisted causal bounds.
The plug-in classification boundary error has the sharp \(1+\alpha\) margin power under sup-norm regression error.
A corrected causal posterior has an efficient Gaussian limit and exact pointwise credible-set coverage under product-rate conditions and strong overlap.
Nondifferentiability in a finite-dimensional local experiment rules out regular locally unbiased estimation.
Ordinary bootstrap validity for a directionally differentiable map requires full differentiability, while a derivative bootstrap can remain valid.

body.tldr: Multiplying a treatment probability and capping it at one defines a support-preserving intervention but introduces a kink at \(e(X)=1/\delta\). The proposal characterizes the exact pathwise-differentiability frontier by the outcome-relevant cap quantity \(K_\delta(P)\), derives the bounded canonical gradient and an exact branch-specific one-step remainder, proves the sharp margin modulus for cap crossings, and establishes pointwise one-step posterior Gaussian calibration and credible-set coverage for an explicit all-data Beta histogram posterior whose draws cross the cap and whose truth violates strong overlap. A legal finite-partition tangent supplies the nonregular converse. Uniform validity under laws drifting across the regularity boundary remains a first-class open question.

project_justification.gap: The capped probability-multiplication policy is already explicit in the interventional-effects literature, but smooth stochastic-intervention efficiency and posterior theorems cannot differentiate through its interior cap. General one-step posterior theory assumes the exact remainder and empirical-process conditions that cap-crossing draws violate, and existing histogram contraction does not cover joint conditional coordinates with unequal random arm counts.
project_justification.niche: The missing object is a complete regularity-and-calibration theory for one identified, positivity-robust stochastic intervention at laws that may touch the cap or the propensity endpoints.
project_justification.fill: The project joins an if-and-only-if regularity theorem, a bounded canonical gradient, an exact crossing remainder with a sharp margin equality example, and a concrete conjugate histogram posterior theorem proved by random-count concentration and boundary-bin localization.

body.related_work: Zhou and Opacic define and motivate multiplicative propensity interventions capped at one; their results are the policy anchor and do not supply a cap-contact regularity analysis. Kennedy derives efficient influence functions and one-step estimation for smooth incremental odds interventions without positivity, supplying the score calculus on each fixed branch. Luedtke and van der Laan give the closest exact exceptional-law differentiability theorem for an optimal treatment value, but their kink is driven by the outcome contrast and has a different cancellation mechanism. Yiu et al. provide the general Bayesian-bootstrap one-step posterior transfer theorem, whose remainder, stability, and empirical-process obligations are verified here for a nonsmooth target. Schmidt and Wikle verify those obligations for twice continuously differentiable stochastic interventions using Taylor and influence-function Lipschitz arguments; the capped map violates both steps. Castillo's strong contraction theorem motivates conjugate histogram coordinates but concerns a single density rather than conditional treatment and outcome laws with unequal arm counts. Levis et al. and Audibert--Tsybakov supply the credited margin-localization technique and classical \(1+\alpha\) exponent; the proposed novelty is the exact capped causal remainder and its overlap-free branch geometry, not the generic exponent. Breunig, Liu, and Yu provide a smooth causal posterior-coverage benchmark under product rates and strong overlap. Hirano--Porter and Fang--Santos inform the nonregular diagnostic and open local-inference question rather than serving as claims the proposal purports to sharpen.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The explicit posterior theorem is intentionally proved first on the canonical law \(X\sim\mathrm{Unif}[0,1]\), \(e(x)=x\), with Bernoulli Lipschitz outcomes. Its early kill test is \(\delta=2\), \(\mu_0=1/4\), and \(\mu_1=3/4\): the deterministic posterior sieve and the empirical-process remainder for the corrected draw must be proved uniformly while retaining all-data fitting and cap crossings. The bin-count calculation gives minimum expected arm count of order \(n/J_n^2\), and the boundary-bin calculation gives at most \(2J_n\rho_n+4\) uncertain bins, so no strong-overlap or no-crossing repair appears necessary. A simulation cannot substitute for this theorem. SoftBART, simultaneous inference over \(\delta\), and uniform inference for triangular arrays approaching cap contact are outside the proved core.
body.honest_scope: The iff regularity theorem, exact remainder, sharp one-step crossing modulus, explicit histogram concentration and empirical-process theorem, and pointwise posterior coverage are all to be proved. The generic \(1+\alpha\) margin exponent, general one-step posterior transfer, smooth stochastic-intervention theory, and generic nondifferentiable bootstrap theory are credited prior art. The sharp local confidence-interval constant and adaptation across regular and nonregular sequences remain explicitly open. Nonregularity rules out regular asymptotically linear Gaussian inference; it does not rule out every root-\(n\)-length confidence procedure.
